registry_schema.label: Design
registry_schema.text: The rate of patients with hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) involving portal vein tumor thrombus (PVTT) is up to 50% in Guangxi province, China. Some of them will receive hepatic resection, especially those with type I or II PVTT. However, 5-years recurrence rate is up to 75% after surgery. Some retrospective studies found postoperative radiotherapy may reduce the rate of recurrence. Moreover, few retrospective studies also found neoadjuvant radiotherapy (PMID: 27317960) may improve overall survival for HCC patients involving type II/III PVTT. However, the safety and efficacy of neoadjuvant raidotherapy for HCC involving type I PVTT is unknown.

registry_schema.text: Repetitive transcranial magnetic stimulation (rTMS) is a new therapeutic tool used in psychiatry. Non-invasive, well tolerated and requiring no premedication, it is performed on an outpatient basis. The principle of this technique is to stimulate the cerebral cortex from an electromagnetic coil placed on the scalp. Unlike electroconvulsive therapy, rTMS induces an electrical current on a well-defined region of the cerebral cortex. In psychiatry, this technique is mainly considered in the treatment of depressive disorders resistant to antidepressant medication. schema.label: Population
schema.text: Adjuvant therapy for pathologic high-risk squamous cell carcinoma of the head and neck. Use the phase III schema. The phase II schema is marked complete.

schema.label: Step 1 registration
schema.text: For oropharyngeal primaries only, mandatory p16 analysis is required before Step 2 registration.

schema.label: Step 2 registration
schema.text: Stratify by Zubrod performance status (0 vs 1) and primary site (oral cavity vs larynx vs hypopharynx vs p16-negative oropharynx). Randomize to Arm 1, Arm 3, and Arm 4 in a 1:1:2 ratio. Arm 2 was dropped after phase II. Required phase III sample size: 480 randomized patients. Protocol treatment must begin within 14 days after Step 2.

arms.label: Arm 1
arms.text: Radiation plus cisplatin. Section 6 and 7: IMRT 60 Gy in 6 weeks (2 Gy x 30 fractions) and cisplatin 40 mg/m2 intravenously weekly for 6 doses.

arms.label: Arm 3
arms.text: Radiation plus docetaxel plus cetuximab. Section 6 and 7: IMRT 60 Gy in 6 weeks, cetuximab loading dose 400 mg/m2 then 250 mg/m2 weekly for 6 doses, and docetaxel 15 mg/m2 weekly for 6 doses. The loading dose is given 4 to 8 days before the first radiation and docetaxel, with no radiation or docetaxel on the loading day.

arms.label: Arm 4
arms.text: Radiation plus cisplatin plus atezolizumab. Section 6 and 7: IMRT 60 Gy in 6 weeks, cisplatin 40 mg/m2 weekly for 6 doses concurrent with radiation, and atezolizumab 1200 mg intravenously every 3 weeks at week -1 (before radiation) and at weeks 3, 6, 9, 12, 15, 18, and 21.

schema.label: Radiation details
schema.text: IMRT is mandatory. Proton therapy is not permitted. IGRT is optional unless reduced margins are used, in which case IGRT is mandatory. PTV_6000 is 60 Gy in 30 fractions. PTV_5600, where used, is 56 Gy in 30 fractions (1.87 Gy). An optional integrated boost, PTV_6600, is 66 Gy in 30 fractions (2.2 Gy). A sequential 3D conformal 6 Gy boost is not permitted.

eligibility: Pathologically proven head and neck squamous cell carcinoma of the oral cavity (lips excluded), p16-negative oropharynx, larynx, or hypopharynx.
Oropharyngeal cancer must be p16-negative on central review before Step 2. Every oropharyngeal primary must consent to mandatory tissue submission for central p16 confirmation.

Gross total surgical resection of the high-risk primary within 63 days before registration. A biopsy under general anesthesia followed by definitive ablative surgery is allowed if that gross total resection is within 63 days. Re-resection for short-interval recurrence or persisting disease after an ablative resection is not eligible.
At least one high-risk pathologic feature: extracapsular nodal extension, or invasive cancer at the primary resection margin (tumor on ink, or tumor in a final separately submitted margin).

Pathologic stage III or IV by AJCC 7th edition, with no distant metastases. History and physical examination by a radiation oncologist or medical oncologist within 84 days before registration. Examination by an ENT or head and neck surgeon before surgery. Laryngopharyngoscopy is recommended but not required. An intraoperative examination is acceptable documentation.

Preoperative head and neck imaging within 84 days before surgery: diagnostic-quality contrast neck CT, or diagnostic-quality contrast PET/CT, and/or diagnostic-quality neck MRI (T1 with gadolinium and T2). The scan is submitted in DICOM via TRIAD and the report is uploaded to Rave. Chest CT or PET/CT that includes the chest, with or without contrast, either within 84 days before surgery or within 120 days before registration.
Zubrod performance status 0 or 1 within 14 days before registration. Age 18 or older. Patients with feeding tubes are eligible.

CBC within 14 days: leukocytes at least 2,500 cells/mm3, absolute neutrophil count at least 1,500 cells/mm3, platelets at least 100,000 cells/mm3, and hemoglobin at least 8.0 g/dL (transfusion or other intervention is allowed).

Hepatic function within 14 days: total bilirubin at or below 1.5 times the institutional upper limit of normal (Gilbert disease may be enrolled at or below 3 times that limit), AST or ALT at or below 3 times that limit, and alkaline phosphatase at or below 2.5 times that limit.

Creatinine clearance at least 50 mL/min within 14 days, by 24-hour collection or Cockcroft-Gault. Negative urine or serum pregnancy test within 14 days for women of childbearing potential. Study-specific informed consent is required before entry.

HIV-positive patients are allowed with a stable HAART regimen, no requirement for concurrent antibiotics or antifungals to prevent opportunistic infections, a CD4 count above 250 cells/mcL, and an undetectable HIV viral load on standard PCR-based tests.

Step 1 is registration. Step 2 is randomization. Oropharynx patients complete Step 2 after central p16 results. Oral cavity, hypopharynx, and larynx patients may complete Step 2 after the Step 1 confirmation email. Protocol treatment starts within 14 days after Step 2.

No prior invasive malignancy unless disease-free for at least 1,095 days (3 years), except non-melanoma skin cancer and resected T1-2 N0 M0 differentiated thyroid carcinoma. Noninvasive cancers, for example carcinoma in situ of the breast, oral cavity, or cervix, are allowed even if diagnosed and treated within 3 years.
Simultaneous primaries or bilateral tumors are excluded, except bilateral tonsil cancers and the resected differentiated thyroid carcinoma exception above.

No prior systemic therapy for the study cancer, including cytotoxic chemotherapy, biologic or targeted therapy such as anti-EGF therapy, or immune therapy. Prior chemotherapy for a different cancer is allowed, but a prior anti-PD-1, anti-PD-L1, or anti-PD-L2 agent is not permitted. No prior radiotherapy to the region of the study cancer that would overlap fields.

Patients with known or current cardiac disease, or prior cardiotoxic agents, must be New York Heart Association class 2B or better within 6 months before registration. No transmural myocardial infarction within 6 months.

No severe infection within 4 weeks before registration, including hospitalization for infection, bacteremia, or severe pneumonia. No acute bacterial or fungal infection requiring intravenous antibiotics at registration. Prophylactic antibiotics, for example for urinary infection or COPD, are allowed. No COPD exacerbation or other respiratory illness requiring hospitalization or precluding study therapy at registration.

No history of idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis, pneumonitis including drug-induced pneumonitis, organizing pneumonia, or active pneumonitis on the screening chest CT. Radiation fibrosis in a prior field is allowed if that field does not overlap the planned study field. Active tuberculosis is excluded.

No known clinically significant liver disease, including active viral, alcoholic, or other hepatitis, cirrhosis, fatty liver, or inherited liver disease. Past or resolved hepatitis B (HBsAg negative and anti-HBc positive) is eligible. HCV antibody is eligible only if PCR is negative for HCV RNA. No allogeneic bone marrow transplant or solid organ transplant. AIDS, by the current CDC definition, is excluded. HIV testing is not required.

No systemic immunosuppressive medication within 2 weeks before registration, including prednisone, cyclophosphamide, azathioprine, methotrexate, thalidomide, and anti-TNF agents. A one-time low dose, such as dexamethasone for nausea, is allowed. Inhaled corticosteroids and mineralocorticoids for orthostatic hypotension or adrenocortical insufficiency are allowed.

History or risk of autoimmune disease is excluded, including systemic lupus erythematosus, rheumatoid arthritis, inflammatory bowel disease, antiphospholipid thrombosis, Wegener granulomatosis, Sjogren syndrome, Guillain-Barre syndrome, multiple sclerosis, vasculitis, and glomerulonephritis. Exceptions: asymptomatic autoimmune hypothyroidism and/or a stable thyroid replacement dose, controlled type 1 diabetes on stable insulin, and eczema, psoriasis, lichen simplex chronicus, or vitiligo limited to the skin if psoriasis has a baseline eye exam excluding ocular disease, rash covers less than 10 percent of body surface area, disease is controlled on low-potency topical steroids only, and there has been no acute exacerbation within 12 months requiring PUVA, methotrexate, retinoids, biologic agents, oral calcineurin inhibitors, or high-potency or oral steroids. Psoriatic arthritis is excluded.

No grade 3 or 4 electrolyte abnormality (CTCAE v4) within 14 days that persists despite intervention: calcium below 7 mg/dL or above 12.5 mg/dL, glucose below 40 mg/dL or above 250 mg/dL, magnesium below 0.9 mg/dL or above 3 mg/dL, potassium below 3.0 mmol/L or above 6 mmol/L, or sodium below 130 mmol/L or above 155 mmol/L.

Pregnancy is excluded. Women of childbearing potential and sexually active men who are unwilling or unable to use medically acceptable contraception for up to 5 months after the last study treatment are excluded. Women who are breastfeeding and unwilling to discontinue are excluded.

No history of severe allergic, anaphylactic, or other hypersensitivity reactions to chimeric or humanized antibodies or fusion proteins. No prior allergic reaction to cisplatin, docetaxel, cetuximab, or atezolizumab. No known hypersensitivity to Chinese hamster ovary cell products or other recombinant human antibodies.

Bisphosphonate therapy for symptomatic hypercalcemia is excluded. Use for other reasons, such as osteoporosis, is allowed. A RANKL inhibitor such as denosumab for a non-oncologic reason must be discontinued before registration if the patient cannot stop it. Known distant metastatic disease is excluded.

No major surgical procedure within 28 days before registration, and no anticipated need for a major surgical procedure during the study. This exclusion does not apply to the cancer resection in section 3.2.3. No live attenuated vaccine within 4 weeks before registration, during the study, or, for patients receiving atezolizumab, until 5 months after the last atezolizumab dose. Live attenuated influenza vaccine is not allowed within 4 weeks before registration or at any time during the study. Psychiatric illness or social situations that would limit compliance are excluded.

schema.text: Phase III trial S0001 (NCT00017147) of radiotherapy plus O6-benzylguanine and BCNU versus radiotherapy plus BCNU in newly diagnosed glioblastoma or gliosarcoma. The primary endpoint was overall survival.

schema.label: Stratify
schema.text: Dynamic balancing by age (under 50 versus 50 or older), Zubrod performance status (0 to 1 versus 2), and surgery (biopsy only versus resection).

schema.label: Randomize
schema.text: Treatment started within five working days of registration. Chemotherapy began concurrently with radiotherapy. A maximum of seven cycles was allowed.

arms.label: O6-BG plus BCNU and radiotherapy
arms.text: O6-BG 120 mg/m2 intravenously over one hour, then six hours later BCNU 40 mg/m2, every six weeks, plus radiotherapy.

arms.label: BCNU and radiotherapy
arms.text: BCNU 200 mg/m2 intravenously over one hour every six weeks, plus radiotherapy.

schema.label: Treatment
schema.text: Radiotherapy was once daily, five days a week, with at least 4 MV photons and multiple conformal fields, without intensity modulation. The initial volume was T2 signal plus a 2 cm margin, treated to 50.4 Gy in 28 fractions. The boost was the resection cavity plus gadolinium enhancement plus a 2.5 cm margin, treated with an additional 10.8 Gy in 6 fractions, for 61.2 Gy cumulative.

brief.schema_source: Trial report, Blumenthal et al., International Journal of Clinical Oncology 2014 (PMID 25407559). Read from the full text.
eligibility: Histologically confirmed glioblastoma or gliosarcoma, age at least 18, Zubrod performance status 2 or better, and biopsy or resection within 28 days before registration.

Adequate renal function (creatinine at or below 1.5 times the upper limit of normal, or creatinine clearance at least 60 mL/min) and PT/PTT at or below 120% of the upper limit of normal. Pulmonary function required DLCO at least 70% of predicted.

Excluded: prior or concurrent cranial radiotherapy or chemotherapy outside the protocol; three or more noncontiguous T2 sites; known allergy to the study drugs; HIV; uncontrolled medical illness; specified prior malignancy; pregnancy or nursing.

schema.text: Metastatic HER2-positive breast cancer on or starting trastuzumab-based therapy, at increased cardiac risk. Baseline ECHO (within 28 days) submitted for central read.

schema.label: Step 2: Registration
schema.text: Central LVEF ≥ 50% confirmed; register within 21 days of ECHO submission. Cohort assigned by current beta blocker, ARB, or ACE inhibitor use.

schema.label: Arm 3: Observation (only arm open)
schema.text: Patients already taking a beta blocker, ARB, or ACE inhibitor continue it; no study drug. Standard-of-care ECHOs (expected every 12 weeks) submitted centrally, with blood specimens, for 108 weeks or until cardiac dysfunction.

schema.label: Closed randomized cohort
schema.text: Patients not on these agents were randomized (stratified by prior anthracycline and central LVEF 50-54% vs ≥ 55%) to Arm 1, carvedilol 6.25 mg PO twice daily for 108 weeks, or Arm 2, no prophylaxis. Arms 1 and 2 are permanently closed to accrual as of Revision 7.

schema.label: Endpoint assessment
schema.text: Cardiac dysfunction by central ECHO Core Lab read and predefined cardiac events; HER2 therapy continuation is at physician discretion.

schema.label: Primary objective
schema.text: 2-year cumulative incidence of cardiac dysfunction and/or predefined cardiac events in patients on trastuzumab-based therapy plus a beta blocker, ARB, or ACE inhibitor, and a risk prediction model from clinical factors and biomarkers.

eligibility: Metastatic breast cancer, starting within 11 days of Step 1 or continuing trastuzumab-based HER2-targeted therapy in the first- to fourth-line metastatic setting (trastuzumab or biosimilar with or without chemotherapy, endocrine therapy, pertuzumab, lapatinib, or tucatinib; T-DM1; trastuzumab deruxtecan). No limit on prior HER2 doses.
No lapatinib without trastuzumab, and no planned concurrent anthracycline with HER2 therapy.
Brain metastases allowed.

Increased cardiotoxicity risk: prior anthracycline, or at least one of LVEF 50-54% on local ECHO, age ≥ 65, BMI ≥ 30, current or prior antihypertensive therapy, coronary artery disease, diabetes, or atrial fibrillation/flutter.
Observation cohort (Arm 3, the only open arm): currently taking a beta blocker, ARB, or ACE inhibitor at Step 1. (Closed randomized arms required no such agent within 21 days.)
LVEF ≥ 50% by 2D or 3D ECHO within 28 days, done at the site's validated ECHO lab and confirmed by central read before Step 2; follow-up ECHOs must include 2D images.
Age ≥ 18; Zubrod performance status 0-2; history and physical within 28 days.
Bilirubin < 3.0 x ULN, AST/ALT < 5.0 x ULN within 28 days; not dialysis dependent.

No other prior malignancy except treated basal or squamous skin cancer, cervical carcinoma in situ, prostate cancer on active surveillance, treated stage I-II cancer in complete remission, or any cancer disease free for 5 years.
Not pregnant and not nursing.
Willing to submit blood specimens.

schema.label: LUNGMAP registration
schema.text: Previously treated stage IV or recurrent NSCLC screened on the Lung-MAP master protocol; not eligible for a biomarker-matched sub-study and assigned to S1800E as a non-match sub-study.

schema.label: Stratify
schema.text: Histology (squamous or mixed vs non-squamous); Zubrod performance status (0 vs 1).

schema.label: Randomize
schema.text: 21-day cycles starting within 7 days of randomization, until progression, unacceptable toxicity, or treatment delay > 84 days. Randomization ratio not stated in the protocol text.

arms.label: Arm A (control)
arms.text: Ramucirumab 10 mg/kg IV Day 1 + docetaxel 75 mg/m2 IV Day 1 (60 mg/m2 allowed) every 21 days, with dexamethasone premedication.

arms.label: Arm B
arms.text: Ramucirumab + docetaxel as in Arm A + cemiplimab 350 mg IV Day 1 every 21 days. Cycle 1 safety run-in with weekly toxicity checks.

schema.label: Primary endpoint
schema.text: Overall survival (phase III), with a phase II interim futility analysis on PFS at 99 events. Accrual goal 378.

schema.label: Follow-up
schema.text: Until death or 3 years after randomization.

eligibility: Registered to LUNGMAP, not eligible for a biomarker-matched sub-study, and assigned to S1800E by the SDMC.
Measurable disease by CT or MRI within 28 days before randomization (non-measurable disease assessed within 42 days). Disease limited to a prior RT port must show clear progression.
Brain CT or MRI within 42 days before randomization.

Exactly one prior anti-PD-1 or anti-PD-L1 regimen for advanced disease; perioperative PD-1/PD-L1 counts if progression occurred ≤ 365 days from its start. Progression > 84 days after starting the most recent PD-1/PD-L1 regimen, with best response of SD, PR, or CR if given for stage IV disease.
Prior platinum-based chemotherapy with progression; at least one prior targeted therapy if an actionable alteration is present.
No prior docetaxel.
No palliative RT within 14 days before randomization (bone RT within 7 days).
No major surgery within 28 days or port placement within 7 days; no wound-healing complications within 2 months; no nonhealing wound or fracture within 28 days.

HIV allowed on effective ART with undetectable viral load within 6 months; HBV and HCV allowed with undetectable viral load within 6 months.
No prior or concurrent malignancy likely to interfere with safety or efficacy assessment.

No transplant requiring immunosuppression, live vaccine within 28 days, active TB, or pneumonitis or ILD that required steroids.

No VTE within 3 months; VTE more than 3 months earlier must be on stable anticoagulation.

Not pregnant or breastfeeding. Agrees to ctDNA blood submission.

Recovered to grade 1 or less from prior therapy toxicity (except alopecia and vitiligo).
Zubrod performance status 0-1 within 28 days before sub-study randomization. Able to swallow tablets whole.

ECG with QTcF of 470 msec or less within 28 days. Urine protein 1+ or less on dipstick or UA (if 2+ or more, 24-hour urine protein below 1000 mg). INR no more than 1.5 seconds and PTT no more than 5 seconds above the institutional ULN unless anticoagulated.
Known HIV allowed if on effective antiretroviral therapy with undetectable viral load within 6 months.
Cardiac history or prior cardiotoxic therapy requires NYHA class 2B or better.

No signs or symptoms of pancreatitis or pancreatic injury (asymptomatic amylase or lipase elevation allowed). No uncontrolled blood pressure or hypertension within 28 days, as judged by the treating investigator.
No moderate or strong CYP3A4 inducers (including St. John's Wort) within 7 days before sub-study registration or during treatment.
No prior or concurrent malignancy whose natural history or treatment could interfere with safety or efficacy assessment.
Not pregnant and not nursing.
Must agree to ctDNA blood submission.

eligibility: Assigned to S1900J by the SWOG SDMC based on NSCLC with MET amplification in LUNGMAP, identified by on-study tumor testing or documented from a prior tissue- or blood-based NGS test on the approved list.
No other known actionable oncogenic alteration (EGFR sensitizing or T790M, MET exon 14 skipping, ALK, ROS1, RET, NTRK, HER2 mutation, KRAS G12C, BRAF V600E, among others).

Measurable disease by CT or MRI within 28 days before sub-study registration (non-measurable sites within 42 days). Effusions, ascites, or labs alone do not qualify. A lesion inside a prior RT port counts as measurable only if clearly progressive.

Brain CT or MRI within 42 days before sub-study registration. Asymptomatic CNS metastases (brain or leptomeningeal) allowed if clinically stable and asymptomatic for at least 14 days; prednisone 10 mg or less (or equivalent) for at least 14 days is allowed.
At least one prior line of systemic therapy for stage IV or recurrent NSCLC, with progression on the most recent line.
No prior MET TKI (tepotinib, capmatinib, crizotinib, etc.) for any cancer.

No systemic therapy (chemotherapy, immunotherapy, investigational drug) within 21 days; no anti-PD-1 or anti-PD-L1 antibody within 6 weeks; no radiation therapy within 14 days before sub-study registration. No planned concurrent chemotherapy, immunotherapy, biologic, or hormonal cancer therapy.
No major surgery (other than vascular access or biopsy) or significant trauma within 28 days, and no surgery planned during the study.
Recovered to grade 1 or less from prior therapy toxicity, except known permanent effects (for example immunotherapy endocrinopathy, cisplatin neurotoxicity).
Zubrod performance status 0-2 within 28 days before sub-study registration.

Within 28 days: ANC at least 1.5 x 10^3/uL, hemoglobin at least 10.0 g/dL, platelets at least 75 x 10^3/uL; total bilirubin up to 1.5 x ULN (up to 5 x ULN with Gilbert's); AST and ALT up to 3 x ULN (up to 5 x ULN with liver metastases); serum creatinine at or below ULN or creatinine clearance at least 45 mL/min (Cockcroft-Gault).
No history of pneumonitis requiring drug therapy and no active symptomatic ILD/pneumonitis, including drug-induced or radiation pneumonitis.

Known HIV allowed if on effective antiretroviral therapy with undetectable viral load within 6 months. Chronic HBV requires undetectable viral load on suppressive therapy within 6 months; HCV must be cured, or undetectable viral load within 6 months if on treatment. No other clinically active infectious liver disease.
Cardiac history or prior cardiotoxic therapy requires NYHA class 2B or better. No clinically significant hypertension within 28 days. Known diabetes must be controlled within 14 days.

No active bleeding diathesis, no continuous oxygen requirement, and no unstable ophthalmologic condition. Infections needing antimicrobials must finish treatment within 7 days before starting study treatment.
No prior or concurrent malignancy whose natural history or treatment could interfere with safety or efficacy assessment.
Not pregnant and not nursing; negative serum pregnancy test within 7 days if of reproductive potential.
Must agree to ctDNA blood submission, and archival tissue (if available) when MET amplification came from a non-Foundation Medicine test.

eligibility: Assigned to S1900K by the SWOG SDMC through the LUNGMAP screening protocol.
Stage IV or recurrent NSCLC with a MET exon 14 skipping mutation by tissue- or blood-based (ctDNA) NGS in a CLIA, ISO/IEC, CAP, or similarly certified laboratory.

arms.text: Observation (visits every 3 months for the first year, then every 6 months) until a 2018 iwCLL treatment indication is met, then venetoclax plus obinutuzumab as below.

schema.label: V-O regimen (both arms)
schema.text: 28-day cycles. Obinutuzumab IV: Cycle 1 100 mg day 1, 900 mg day 2, 1000 mg days 8 and 15; 1000 mg day 1 of Cycles 2-6, then stop. Venetoclax PO with 5-week ramp-up: 20 mg days 22-28 of Cycle 1, then 50, 100, 200, 400 mg weekly in Cycle 2, then 400 mg daily through Cycle 12, then stop. TLS risk assessment and prophylaxis required.

eligibility: Confirmed CLL or SLL by 2018 iwCLL criteria, diagnosed within 18 months before registration.
CLL-IPI score of 4 or higher and/or complex cytogenetics (3 or more chromosomal abnormalities).

Cytogenetics and/or FISH (at minimum 13q, 12, 11q, 17p probes) in a CLIA-approved or Accreditation Canada laboratory within 18 months before registration; TP53 mutation analysis, if done, within 18 months; IGHV mutation status any time before registration; serum beta-2 microglobulin within 28 days.
Does not meet any iwCLL criterion for active CLL therapy.

No prior CLL-directed therapy of any kind, including immunotherapy, experimental therapy, or radiotherapy; no prior anti-CD20 antibody; no other investigational agents planned before completing protocol therapy.

High-dose corticosteroids or IVIG for autoimmune complications of CLL completed at least 4 weeks before enrollment; steroids for other conditions no more than prednisone 20 mg/day (or equivalent) at registration.
Age 18 or older; ECOG performance status 0-2; able to take oral medication.

Within 28 days: platelets at least 100,000/mm3, ANC at least 1,000/mm3, creatinine clearance at least 30 mL/min (Cockcroft-Gault), AST and ALT below 3.0 x ULN, total bilirubin up to 2.0 x ULN (5.0 x ULN with Gilbert's).

No prior malignancy requiring active treatment within 2 years (hormonal therapy allowed); exceptions include non-melanoma skin cancer, cervical carcinoma in situ, superficial bladder cancer without intravesical therapy within 6 months, localized prostate cancer treated with surgery and/or radiation only or on chronic hormonal therapy, Gleason 6 or lower prostate cancer, and localized breast cancer treated with surgery and/or radiation only or on chronic hormonal therapy.

No uncontrolled active hepatitis B or C (detectable HBV DNA or HCV RNA). Latent hepatitis B requires antiviral prophylaxis during and for 6 months after V-O. HIV allowed if on effective antiretroviral therapy with undetectable viral load within 6 months.
No cirrhosis and no clinically significant GI malabsorption.
No major surgery within 30 days or minor surgery within 7 days before registration (diagnostic bone marrow biopsy allowed).
No known bleeding disorder; no stroke or intracranial hemorrhage within 6 months.
No ongoing need for a strong CYP3A4/5 inhibitor or inducer.
No uncontrolled autoimmune hemolytic anemia or ITP.
No active clinically significant cardiovascular disease (for example uncontrolled arrhythmia or NYHA class 3-4 heart failure); no MI, unstable angina, or acute coronary syndrome within 6 months.
Not pregnant and not nursing.
Must agree to MRD specimen submission.

schema.text: Newly diagnosed metastatic RCC with primary tumor in place. Enter either immunotherapy-naive (start pre-randomization treatment within 7 days) or after completing the protocol-specified pre-randomization regimen off protocol (Step 1 and Step 2 the same day).

schema.text: Nivolumab 3 mg/kg plus ipilimumab 1 mg/kg q3 weeks (up to 4 doses), then nivolumab 240 mg q2 weeks or 480 mg q4 weeks; nivolumab (240 mg q2 weeks or 480 mg q4 weeks) plus cabozantinib 40 mg daily; pembrolizumab (200 mg q3 weeks or 400 mg q6 weeks) plus axitinib 5 mg BID; pembrolizumab plus lenvatinib 20 mg daily; or avelumab (800 mg or 10 mg/kg q2 weeks) plus axitinib 5 mg BID.

No other prior malignancy except adequately treated basal or squamous cell skin cancer, in situ (Step 1 also T1) cancer, adequately treated stage I or II cancer in complete remission, or other cancer disease-free for at least 2 years.

Step 2: Restaging CT chest and CT or MRI abdomen/pelvis 12 weeks (plus or minus 2 weeks) after starting pre-randomization therapy and within 28 days before randomization, showing stable disease, partial response, or investigator-judged clinical benefit with Zubrod 0-1. Complete response in all metastatic sites is not eligible.
Step 2: No progression in metastatic sites or primary tumor (pseudoprogression allowed); plans to continue the same immune-based regimen.

Step 2: Randomized between week 11 day 1 and week 14 day 7 of pre-randomization treatment, after at least the minimum immunotherapy (for example 2 nivolumab plus 1 ipilimumab infusion, 2 pembrolizumab 200 mg or 1 pembrolizumab 400 mg, or 2 avelumab infusions).

Step 2: Zubrod performance status 0-1 and history and physical within 28 days before randomization.
Step 2: Within 28 days: total bilirubin up to 2 x ULN; AST and ALT up to 3 x ULN (up to 5 x ULN with liver metastases); serum creatinine up to 1.5 x ULN or creatinine clearance at least 50 mL/min.

Step 1: At least one indication for therapy: anemia, thrombocytopenia, WM-related neuropathy, symptomatic hyperviscosity or serum viscosity at least 4.0 cP, WM-associated glomerulonephritis or renal disease, bulky disease, or constitutional symptoms. Smoldering WM is not eligible.
Step 1: No prior systemic therapy; prior rituximab allowed if the last dose was at least 6 months before registration. Not intolerant to rituximab.

schema.label: Registration
schema.text: Advanced or metastatic poorly differentiated extrapulmonary neuroendocrine carcinoma. Treatment starts within 7 calendar days of registration.

schema.label: Stratification
schema.text: Zubrod 0-1 vs 2; tumor origin: prostate vs GI vs other (non-prostate, non-GI, or unknown).

schema.label: Randomize 1:1:1
schema.text: Induction is 4 cycles of 21 days. Platinum is physician's choice: carboplatin AUC 5 or cisplatin 75 mg/m2 IV day 1, with etoposide 100 mg/m2 IV days 1-3. A single pre-registration cycle of platinum/etoposide does not count toward the 4.

arms.label: Arm 1 (experimental)
arms.text: Atezolizumab 1,200 mg IV day 1 plus platinum/etoposide for 4 cycles; if no progression, maintenance atezolizumab 1,200 mg IV every 21 days for up to 17 cycles (maximum 1 year).

arms.label: Arm 2 (experimental, closed)
arms.text: Atezolizumab plus platinum/etoposide for 4 cycles, then observation for 1 year. Permanently closed to accrual effective July 9, 2026; new participants are randomized to Arm 1 or Arm 3 only.

arms.label: Arm 3 (control)
arms.text: Platinum/etoposide for 4 cycles, then observation for 1 year.

schema.text: Until death or 5 years after registration, whichever comes first.

schema.label: Primary endpoint
schema.text: Overall survival from randomization, tested in fixed sequence: Arm 1 vs Arm 3, then Arm 2 vs Arm 3, then Arm 1 vs Arm 2.

eligibility: Histologically confirmed extrapulmonary poorly differentiated neuroendocrine carcinoma by WHO criteria, with Ki-67 of 55% or higher (Ki-67 not required for genitourinary origin); local pathology confirmation is sufficient.

Unresectable or metastatic disease not eligible for definitive therapy, with RECIST-evaluable (measurable or non-measurable) disease on contrast CT chest/abdomen/pelvis (or CT chest plus MRI abdomen/pelvis) within 28 days before registration. PET or bone scan alone is not acceptable.

Brain MRI (or contrast head CT) within 28 days only if clinically indicated. No symptomatic CNS metastases and no known or suspected leptomeningeal disease. Treated brain metastases need no progression within 28 days and steroids stopped at least 14 days; untreated lesions must be 2.0 cm or smaller, without mass effect, edema, or progression, and need no more than dexamethasone 2 mg/day (or prednisone 10 mg).

No prior therapy for advanced or metastatic NEC except one cycle of platinum plus etoposide. Prior platinum-based therapy with or without radiation or surgery for localized or locally advanced NEC allowed if completed at least 6 months before registration. Prostate or urothelial NEC: prior chemotherapy for the non-NEC component allowed if completed at least 24 weeks before registration.

No prior immune checkpoint inhibitor (anti-PD-1, PD-L1, PD-L2, CTLA-4, CD137 agonist, or other) for any neuroendocrine neoplasm; checkpoint inhibitors for other cancers allowed if the last dose was at least 12 months before registration. No systemic immunostimulatory agents (interferon, IL-2) within 4 weeks or 5 half-lives.

No active systemic therapy for another cancer except hormonal therapy (ADT may continue; enzalutamide or apalutamide only after chemotherapy; darolutamide allowed during chemotherapy; no abiraterone or other glucocorticoid-containing regimens). Denosumab must be stopped and replaced with a bisphosphonate.
Age 18 or older; Zubrod performance status 0-2 within 28 days.

Within 14 days (at least 21 days after day 1 of any pre-registration chemotherapy cycle): ANC at least 1.5 x 10^9/L, hemoglobin at least 9.0 g/dL, platelets at least 100 x 10^9/L, AST and ALT up to 2.5 x ULN, total bilirubin up to 1.5 x ULN, creatinine clearance above 50 mL/min. No uncontrolled or symptomatic hypercalcemia.
No immunodeficiency and no systemic steroids above hydrocortisone 20 mg/day equivalent or other immunosuppression within 14 days.
No active or prior autoimmune disease, except hypothyroidism on replacement, controlled type 1 diabetes on insulin, and limited skin-only eczema, psoriasis, lichen simplex chronicus, or vitiligo.

No idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis, organizing pneumonia, drug-induced or idiopathic pneumonitis, or active pneumonitis on screening CT (radiation pneumonitis confined to the radiation field is allowed).
No NYHA class II or higher heart disease, MI within 3 months, unstable arrhythmia, or unstable angina.
No major surgery (other than diagnostic) within 28 days or planned during treatment. No grade 2 or higher infection at registration and no known active tuberculosis.
Chronic HBV requires undetectable viral load; HCV must be cured or undetectable on treatment; known HIV requires effective antiretroviral therapy with undetectable viral load within 6 months.
No prior allogeneic stem cell or solid organ transplant. No live attenuated vaccine within 28 days before treatment, during atezolizumab, or for 5 months after.
No severe hypersensitivity to chimeric or humanized antibodies, CHO cell products, atezolizumab, cisplatin, carboplatin, or etoposide.
Not pregnant.

schema.label: Design
schema.text: Single-arm phase II immunoMATCH pilot (BiCaZO) of cabozantinib plus nivolumab in PD-1 refractory melanoma or HNSCC. Two disease cohorts (melanoma, HNSCC), each stratified by tumor inflammation score (TIS): TIS high is 6 or more for melanoma and 7 or more for HNSCC. TMB is measured but no longer used for cohort assignment.

schema.label: Step 1: Specimen submission
schema.text: Order kits one week before registration. Submit fresh biopsy or archival tissue plus blood within 3 days after Step 1 registration for central TMB and TIS testing.

schema.label: Step 2: Treatment registration
schema.text: Stage I: registered and treated before biomarker results, assigned to biomarker cohort retrospectively. Stage II (opened with Revision #5): registered only if a slot is open in the participant's biomarker cohort; otherwise off study. Treatment starts within 7 days of Step 2 registration.

schema.label: Treatment
schema.text: Nivolumab 480 mg IV day 1 every 28 days plus cabozantinib 40 mg PO daily, fasting (no food 2 hours before and 1 hour after). Up to 24 months or 26 cycles. Treatment beyond initial RECIST progression allowed during the first 24 weeks if clinically stable and benefiting.

schema.label: Follow-up
schema.text: Until death or 3 years after Step 2 registration.

schema.label: Accrual
schema.text: Through September 30, 2027 or until 220 participants are screened, whichever comes first.

schema.label: Primary endpoints
schema.text: Feasibility: proportion with biomarker turnaround of 21 days or less (Stage I TMB; Stage II TMB and TIS), with at least 75% considered feasible. Efficacy: ORR in each disease cohort by TIS subgroup.

eligibility: Step 1: Histologically confirmed unresectable stage III or IV, recurrent, or metastatic non-uveal melanoma; or HNSCC of the oropharynx, oral cavity, hypopharynx, or larynx that is metastatic or locally recurrent and not amenable to curative therapy. No nasopharynx primary or unknown primary. HPV or p16 status known for oropharynx.
Step 1: Disease consistent with measurable disease.

Step 1: Documented progression during or within 12 weeks after the last dose of PD-1 based therapy, after at least 6 weeks of checkpoint inhibitor. Recurrence during or within 12 weeks of adjuvant anti-PD-1 qualifies if measurable and unresectable.
Step 1: Recovered to baseline or grade 1 or less from prior treatment toxicity (unless clinically nonsignificant or stable on supportive therapy).

Step 1: No more than one prior curative or adjuvant RT course to head and neck mucosal surfaces, completed at least 16 weeks before (chemoradiation) or 8 weeks before (RT alone). Step 1: No prior anti-VEGF therapy.
Step 1: Age 18 or older; Zubrod 0-1; NYHA class 2B or better if cardiac history or prior cardiotoxic therapy; able to swallow capsules whole; no malabsorption.
Step 1: No MI or thromboembolic event requiring anticoagulation within 90 days unless stable on management. No uncontrolled hypertension (systolic over 150 or diastolic over 90 mmHg) within 28 days.

Step 1: No hemoptysis (1/2 teaspoon or more of bright red blood) or tumor bleeding within 90 days. No prior carotid bleeding, tumor invading major vessels, cavitary central lung metastases (within 2 cm of hilum), or bleeding from the current head and neck cancer.

Step 1: No warfarin, direct thrombin inhibitors, betrixaban, or platelet inhibitors such as clopidogrel. Low-dose aspirin and prophylactic LMWH allowed; therapeutic LMWH, rivaroxaban, edoxaban, or apixaban allowed if no known brain metastases and stable dose for at least 1 week.

Step 1: No active autoimmune disease requiring more than 10 mg prednisone equivalent or other immunosuppression (type 1 diabetes, replaced endocrinopathy, and non-systemically treated skin disorders allowed). No organ allograft. No active infection requiring systemic therapy.

Step 1: HIV allowed with undetectable viral load within 6 months on ART. Chronic HBV allowed with undetectable viral load within 28 days; prior HCV allowed with undetectable viral load within 28 days.
Step 1: Adequate archival tissue obtained after resistance to anti-PD-1/L1, or fresh biopsy with under 2% expected risk of severe complications; whole blood for germline analysis.
Step 1: Not pregnant and not nursing.
Step 2: Still meets Step 1 criteria; tissue submitted; Stage II participants assigned to an open cohort.
Step 2: Measurable disease assessed within 28 days (non-measurable within 42 days). Melanoma: CT chest, abdomen, and pelvis. HNSCC: CT neck and chest.
Step 2: Treated brain metastases without progression after CNS-directed therapy and off steroids at least 14 days.

Step 2: No surgery, chemotherapy, radiation therapy, biologic agents, or steroids within 14 days; no investigational agents or monoclonal antibodies within 28 days; no live vaccine within 30 days; no strong CYP3A4 inducers within 14 days or strong inhibitors within 5 half-lives.

Step 2: H&P within 28 days. Within 28 days: leukocytes at least 3,000/uL, ANC at least 1,500/uL, platelets at least 100,000/uL, total bilirubin up to 1.5 x ULN (3 x ULN with Gilbert's), AST and ALT up to 3 x ULN, creatinine clearance at least 30 mL/min (Cockcroft-Gault), baseline urinalysis.

No planned warfarin during protocol treatment (other anticoagulants allowed).

No prior or concurrent malignancy that could interfere with safety or efficacy assessment.
No active or uncontrolled infection; no serious medical or psychiatric illness affecting participation.
Not pregnant.

schema.text: Dara-VCD x 3 cycles (28 days): bortezomib 1.3 mg/m2 SC, cyclophosphamide 300 mg/m2 PO/IV (cap 500 mg), dexamethasone 20 mg, all days 1, 8, 15, 22; daratumumab-hyaluronidase 1800 mg SC weekly Cycles 1-2, days 1 and 15 Cycle 3. Start within 14 days

schema.text: Requires at least PR after induction; register within 42 days of C3D28; consolidation within 56 days

arms.text: 3 more cycles of VCD with daratumumab-hyaluronidase 1800 mg SC days 1 and 15

arms.label: Arm 2: Melphalan + ASCT
arms.text: G-CSF (with or without plerixafor) mobilization, no chemo-mobilization, minimum 2.0 x 10^6 CD34+/kg; melphalan 200 mg/m2 (140 mg/m2 allowed, recommended for GFR 30-60) then autologous stem cell transplant

schema.label: Step 3: Maintenance (both arms)
schema.text: Daratumumab-hyaluronidase 1800 mg SC day 1 every 28 days x 18 cycles

schema.label: Follow-up
schema.text: Until death or 7 years from Step 1 registration

schema.label: Primary endpoint
schema.text: Major organ deterioration progression-free survival (MOD-PFS)

eligibility: Age >= 18; ECOG performance status 0-2 (3 allowed if due to neuropathy).
Biopsy-proven systemic AL amyloidosis (Congo red with green birefringence or characteristic EM) with confirmatory typing by mass spectrometry or immunofluorescence.

Measurable disease (monoclonal serum or urine immunofixation or clonal marrow plasma cells) plus dFLC >= 2 mg/dL, assessed within 28 days before therapy (56 days if treatment started before registration).
Up to one cycle (28 days) of any plasma cell-directed therapy before enrollment; no MOD-PFS event if prior Dara-VCD counts toward induction.

Transplant eligible for melphalan 140-200 mg/m2 and willing to undergo ASCT: supine SBP >= 90 mmHg; NT-proBNP < 5000 pg/mL (or BNP < 400); cTnT < 0.06 ng/mL (or hsTnT < 75 ng/L or TnI < 0.1 ng/mL); NYHA I-II; LVEF >= 40%.

Within 56 days: Hb > 8.0 g/dL, WBC >= 2,000/uL, ANC >= 1,000/uL, platelets >= 50,000/uL, bilirubin <= 1.5 x ULN, direct bilirubin <= 2.0 mg/dL, AST/ALT <= 3 x ULN, alkaline phosphatase <= 750 U/L (hepatic involvement excepted), creatinine <= ULN or CrCl >= 30 mL/min.
Peripheral neuropathy grade <= 2.
No concurrent multiple myeloma (lytic lesions, plasmacytoma, >= 60% marrow plasma cells, or hypercalcemia).
No HBsAg positivity or detectable HBV DNA; HCV treated and cured or undetectable within 6 months; HIV on ART with undetectable viral load within 6 months.
No COPD with FEV1 < 50% predicted; no moderate or severe persistent asthma within 2 years or uncontrolled asthma.
No uncontrolled diabetes, hypertension, or infection; no major surgery within 14 days; no live vaccine within 28 days.
No prior or concurrent malignancy that could interfere with safety or efficacy assessment.
Not pregnant or nursing.

Step 2: At least PR after 3 cycles, no MOD-PFS event, still receiving daratumumab plus at least one other study drug; cardiac criteria rechecked within 14 days and labs within 28 days; ASCT arm must collect >= 2.0 x 10^6 CD34+/kg.
Step 3: Daratumumab not permanently discontinued; registered within 28 days of completing Arm 1 consolidation or within 180 days of ASCT; no MOD-PFS event.

Histologically confirmed MSS, HER2-negative gastric, GEJ, or esophageal adenocarcinoma, metastatic or unresectable; PD-L1 CPS >= 1 on tissue obtained within 2 years.
Imaging within 28 days (measurable disease) or 42 days (non-measurable disease).
Treated brain metastases allowed if stable and treatment completed >= 28 days before registration.

Progression on or intolerance of frontline chemotherapy plus PD-1/PD-L1 inhibitor; perioperative chemo-immunotherapy counts as a line if progression occurred within 6 months of completion. No more than 1 prior line in the stage IV setting; RT or regional therapy does not count as a line.
No systemic steroids > 10 mg/day prednisone equivalent or other immunosuppressants within 14 days.
No prior immunotherapy toxicity requiring permanent discontinuation and no grade 3-4 immune-related toxicity (endocrine or thyroid toxicity excepted).
No live vaccine within 28 days; no major surgery within 28 days or port placement within 7 days; no postoperative bleeding or wound complications within 8 weeks; no planned major surgery.

No active bleeding; no GI perforation, fistula, or significant GI bleeding (requiring transfusion or intervention) within 84 days; no grade 3-4 allergic reaction to humanized or human monoclonal antibodies.
No concurrent chemotherapy, immunotherapy, investigational, biologic, or hormonal cancer therapy.

Urine protein <= 1+ by dipstick or urinalysis; if >= 2+, 24-hour urine protein < 1000 mg.
NYHA class 2 or better if cardiac history or prior cardiotoxic therapy; recovered to baseline or < grade 2 from prior therapy toxicity unless stable on supportive therapy.
No arterial thromboembolic event within 6 months; no uncontrolled hypertension within 28 days.

HIV on effective ART with undetectable viral load within 6 months; chronic HBV with undetectable viral load on suppressive therapy within 6 months; HCV treated and cured, or undetectable viral load within 6 months if on treatment.

No inflammatory bowel disease, symptomatic autoimmune disease, or CNS or motor neuropathy of autoimmune origin (Graves' disease allowed); no pneumonitis requiring oral or IV steroids within 12 months.
No prior or concurrent malignancy that could interfere with safety or efficacy assessment.
Not pregnant or nursing.

eligibility: Step 1: histologically or pathologically confirmed extensive-stage small cell lung cancer. No prior or concurrent malignancy whose history or treatment could interfere with safety or efficacy assessment. No history of limited-stage small cell lung cancer.

Step 1 therapy: treatment-naive and planning platinum plus etoposide with durvalumab, or already started and completed at least 1 and at most 3 cycles of platinum and etoposide, of which at most 2 cycles were without durvalumab. No immunotherapy other than durvalumab before enrollment. No prior anti-PD-1 or anti-PD-L1 for small cell lung cancer except durvalumab during this induction. No atezolizumab, pembrolizumab, or nivolumab in frontline induction.

Step 1: no prophylactic cranial irradiation, no investigational agent for extensive-stage disease, and no concurrent non-protocol chemotherapy, immunotherapy, biologic, or hormonal therapy. Bisphosphonates are allowed for bone metastases. No unresolved CTCAE grade 2 or higher toxicity from prior anticancer therapy, except alopecia and vitiligo.

Step 1 clinical: age 18 or older, able to receive platinum, etoposide, and durvalumab, and Zubrod 0-2 within 28 days. Recovered from prior surgery in the investigator's opinion. No allogeneic organ transplant. No contraindication to immunotherapy, including non-infectious pneumonitis that required steroids or active autoimmune disease requiring systemic treatment in the past two years. Replacement therapy such as thyroxine or insulin is allowed.

Step 1: not pregnant or nursing. People of reproductive potential use effective contraception during protocol therapy and for 6 months after, and do not breastfeed during therapy and for 6 months after.

Step 1 tissue: adequate small cell lung cancer tissue for BostonGene per section 15.2, with leftover tissue kept for future studies. After Step 1, submit tissue to BostonGene. Do not register to Step 2 until SWOG notifies the site of the cohort assignment. Cohort B is closed to assignment as of 21 Jan 2026.

Step 2: BostonGene has confirmed subtype A, N, I, or P and assigned a cohort. Measurable or non-measurable disease per RECIST 1.1, assessed by CT of the chest, abdomen, and pelvis within 28 days if measurable or within 42 days if non-measurable. All known sites are documented. A non-diagnostic PET/CT makes those lesions non-measurable.

Step 2 brain: CT or MRI of the brain within 42 days. No leptomeningeal disease, spinal cord compression, or symptomatic brain metastases unless the metastases were locally treated, have stayed clinically controlled and asymptomatic for at least 14 days, there is no residual neurological dysfunction, and corticosteroids have been stopped for at least 24 hours. Untreated brain metastases must be asymptomatic and stable off steroids. Allowed steroid exceptions are intranasal, inhaled, topical, or local injection; physiologic doses up to 10 mg/day of prednisone or equivalent; and steroid premedication.

Step 2 therapy: no progression during induction in the treating investigator's opinion. Frontline induction of 4-6 cycles of platinum plus etoposide with durvalumab is complete, and Step 2 is no more than 8 weeks after the last induction dose. No atezolizumab, pembrolizumab, nivolumab, or prophylactic cranial irradiation.

Step 2 clinical, within 28 days: history and physical, body weight greater than 30 kg, and Zubrod 0-2. Hemoglobin greater than 9.0 g/dL, ANC at least 1.5 x 10^3/uL, platelets at least 100 x 10^3/uL, total bilirubin up to the institutional ULN (up to 5 x ULN with Gilbert disease), and AST/ALT up to 5 x institutional ULN. Creatinine up to 1.5 x ULN or creatinine clearance at least 45 mL/min.
Step 2 infection history: known HIV requires effective antiretroviral therapy and an undetectable viral load within 6 months. Known chronic hepatitis B requires an undetectable viral load.

No uncontrolled hypertension (all readings within 28 days SBP ≤140 and DBP ≤90) and no clinically significant uncontrolled cardiovascular disease within 28 days.
No active autoimmune disease that prohibits immune checkpoint therapy.

schema.text: Bladder radiotherapy plus pembrolizumab for 1 year. Central radiation-plan approval is required before treatment starts. Radiotherapy is whole bladder only, 55 Gy in 20 fractions of 2.75 Gy, with no pelvic nodes and no tumor boost.

eligibility: Histologic cT2-T4aN0M0 muscle-invasive urothelial carcinoma of the bladder within 180 days before neoadjuvant therapy starts. Staging CT, MRI, or PET of the chest, abdomen, and pelvis within 60 days before neoadjuvant therapy.

After neoadjuvant therapy, a repeat TURBT must show cT0 or cT1. It biopsies the prior disease and systematic sites (left and right lateral walls, dome, posterior wall, and trigone), with at least 4 of 5 systematic biopsies. The TURBT is within 60 days after the last neoadjuvant dose and within 90 days before registration.

No cT2 or higher, N1-3, or M1 disease after neoadjuvant therapy. A node of 1.0 cm or larger in short axis after neoadjuvant therapy needs PET-CT within 70 days before registration. A PET-positive node is ineligible unless biopsy shows no tumor.

At least 3 and no more than 6 cycles of FDA-approved neoadjuvant therapy: cisplatin-based combination chemotherapy, with or without a PD-1/L1 inhibitor; dose-dense or accelerated MVAC; or enfortumab vedotin with a PD-1/L1 inhibitor.
No small cell, neuroendocrine, or plasmacytoid histology. Mixed histology is allowed when more than half of the tumor is urothelial carcinoma. No prior pelvic radiotherapy.
The primary objective is written for clinically T0 or T1 disease without multifocal CIS. That CIS phrase is not an eligibility criterion.

eligibility: Age ≥18, Zubrod PS 0-2.
Histologically or cytologically confirmed pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma, unresectable and/or metastatic on CT or MRI (within 28 days if measurable disease, within 42 days if non-measurable only).
Documented KRAS wild type (no KRAS mutation) and BRAF V600E wild type by tumor tissue NGS in a certified lab, confirmed by a study chair before registration; ctDNA/liquid biopsy not accepted.
No known PTEN, NRAS, or EGFR extracellular domain (exons 1-16) mutations, HER2 or MET amplification, or RET, NTRK1, or ALK fusions; untested patients are eligible.

Exactly one prior line of cytotoxic chemotherapy for locally advanced or metastatic disease with progression, refractoriness, or intolerance. No prior anti-EGFR antibody (cetuximab, panitumumab) or EGFR TKI.
No pancreatic cancer therapy (chemotherapy, targeted therapy, or radiation) within 14 days before randomization.
No known brain metastases or cranial epidural disease unless treated with RT and/or surgery and stable ≥28 days, neurologically asymptomatic, and off corticosteroids.
No contraindication to the chosen chemotherapy backbone at planned doses.

No prior or concurrent malignancy that could interfere with safety or efficacy assessment.
Not pregnant and not nursing.

schema.text: Safety run-in: safety. Randomized: investigator-assessed PFS, then OS by hierarchical testing.

eligibility: Age ≥18, ECOG/Zubrod PS 0-2.
Richter transformation (CLL/SLL to LBCL) with histologically or cytologically confirmed LBCL.
Measurable disease by PET/CT or hematopathology (morphology or flow) and staging PET/CT within 42 days before registration.

Prior CLL/SLL therapy allowed except pirtobrutinib. No prior treatment for Richter transformation except corticosteroids up to prednisone 700 mg total for <7 days; CLL-directed drugs after RT diagnosis allowed for disease control (targeted agents stopped 3 days and chemotherapy or anti-CD20 stopped 2 weeks before protocol therapy).
No contraindication to anthracycline; prior doxorubicin-equivalent ≤100 mg/m² for R-CHOP or ≤250 mg/m² for R-mini-CHOP.
No required strong CYP3A inducer unless an alternative exists and the last dose is ≥7 days before pirtobrutinib.

Labs within 28 days: ANC ≥0.75 x 10^3/µL (≥0.50 with marrow involvement), platelets ≥50 x 10^3/µL (≥30 with marrow involvement), hemoglobin ≥8 g/dL (≥6 with marrow involvement), total bilirubin ≤1.5x ULN (≤3x with liver involvement or Gilbert's), AST/ALT ≤3x ULN (≤5x with liver involvement), creatinine clearance ≥30 mL/min.
LVEF ≥45% by echocardiogram or MUGA within 56 days; NYHA class 2B or better if cardiac history or prior cardiotoxic therapy.
No major bleeding event or grade ≥3 arrhythmia on prior BTK inhibitor therapy.
No major surgery within 28 days.
Able to swallow oral medication with no GI disorder likely to impair absorption.

HIV allowed with effective ART (no pirtobrutinib interactions) and undetectable viral load within 6 months; chronic HBV allowed with undetectable viral load on suppressive therapy; HCV must be cured or have undetectable viral load on treatment.
No other prior or concurrent malignancy (beyond CLL/SLL and Richter transformation) that could interfere with safety or efficacy assessment.
Must agree to required blood and lymph node tissue submission for the integrated translational study.
Not pregnant and not nursing.

schema.label: Randomize 1:1
schema.text: Surgery 22-56 days after radiation is completed.

arms.label: Arm 1: RT-25
arms.text: 50 Gy in 25 fractions, then resection.

arms.label: Arm 2: UHRT-5
arms.text: 30 Gy in 5 fractions, then resection.

eligibility: Histologic soft tissue sarcoma on core or incisional biopsy, primary or locally recurrent, stage II-IIIB by AJCC 8th edition. No prior partial excision or partial excisional biopsy, even with gross residual disease. No prior procedure that removed the tumor completely with no gross residual disease.

Primary site in the extremity, including the shoulder girdle and hip girdle, excluding the hands and feet. Trunk, head, neck, intra-abdominal, intrapelvic, and retroperitoneal primaries are excluded. Extension from an eligible primary into an adjacent region such as the torso, hands, or feet is allowed.
MRI of the primary site within 90 days before randomization. The field of view contains the whole tumor and includes axial T1 with fat suppression and a T1 sequence with gadolinium.

Pulmonary nodules 5 mm or smaller without histology are not exclusionary. Nodules of 6-10 mm are allowed if stable for at least 6 months or if FDG-PET makes metastasis unlikely. Nodules larger than 10 mm are treated as metastatic unless biopsy, resection, or 6 months of stability shows otherwise.
No fungating tumor. No myxoid liposarcoma, embryonal rhabdomyosarcoma, alveolar rhabdomyosarcoma, gastrointestinal stromal tumor, osteosarcoma, or NTRK-rearranged spindle cell sarcoma.

A surgeon has judged, within 35 days before randomization, that limb-salvage resection with an expectation of negative margins is appropriate. Anticipated positive margins on fixed critical structures are allowed. No prior treatment of this tumor with systemic therapy, radiation, or complete resection, and no prior radiation to the anatomic site.
Age 18 or older, Zubrod 0-2, and a history and physical within 28 days before randomization that describes the tumor site, laterality, and extremity.
People of reproductive potential use effective contraception. No uncontrolled intercurrent illness that would limit compliance or safety.
Sites in the United States offer optional specimen banking. Informed consent is required. A legally authorized representative may consent when decision-making is impaired.

eligibility: Age ≥18, Zubrod PS 0-2.

Histologically diagnosed CD20+ MZL (splenic, nodal, or extranodal) per WHO; excludes GI-only MZL assessable only by endoscopy and cutaneous-only MZL. Repeat biopsy required only after prior CD3/CD20 bispecific (to document CD20+ MZL); splenic MZL needs bone marrow biopsy within 42 days.
Measurable disease by PET-CT (preferred) or CT (extranodal ≥1 cm or nodal ≥1.5 cm); splenic MZL eligible if spleen SUV > liver background and/or spleen >13 cm. Staging imaging within 42 days.

Needs systemic therapy: symptomatic or bulky nodal disease, organ-threatening progression, B symptoms, symptomatic extranodal disease, cytopenias from marrow infiltration or hypersplenism, or accelerating tempo.

No known or suspected transformation to DLBCL or high-grade B-cell lymphoma (prior transformation now relapsed as MZL only is allowed). CNS involvement allowed if not progressing or CNS-directed treatment not needed during the first 8 cycles.
Relapsed/refractory after ≥1 prior CD20-directed systemic therapy; prior antibiotics or radiation for localized MZL allowed and do not count as a line.
Prior BTK inhibitor or CD3/CD20 bispecific allowed only if completed ≥180 days before registration with best response PR or CR. No prior polatuzumab vedotin.
No CAR-T within 28 days, autologous SCT within 100 days, or allogeneic SCT within 180 days; no active GVHD needing ≥10 mg prednisone; no active PTLD.

No systemic corticosteroids ≥10 mg prednisone equivalent or other immunosuppressants within 7 days (replacement or short-term premedication allowed). Strong/moderate CYP3A4 inducers stopped 14 days or 5 half-lives before registration. Prior-therapy toxicity recovered to <grade 2 (except alopecia, lymphopenia).

Labs within 28 days: ANC ≥1.0 x 10^3/uL (≥0.5 with marrow involvement or Duffy-null), platelets ≥75 x 10^3/uL (≥50 with marrow or splenic involvement), total bilirubin <1.5x ULN (≤5x with Gilbert's), AST/ALT ≤3x ULN, creatinine clearance ≥30 mL/min, INR <2x ULN.
No warfarin or other vitamin K antagonist within 7 days; no severe bleeding disorder or spontaneous bleeding needing intervention; no stroke or intracranial hemorrhage within 180 days.
No history of PML; no uncontrolled AIHA or ITP; no uncontrolled intercurrent illness (infection, autoimmune disease, arrhythmia, angina, neuropathy, hypertension, malabsorption).
NYHA class 2B or better if cardiac history or prior cardiotoxic therapy.

HIV allowed with effective ART and undetectable viral load within 180 days; chronic HBV allowed with undetectable viral load on suppressive therapy (HBcAb-positive patients need antiviral prophylaxis); HCV must be cured or have undetectable viral load on treatment.
No live or attenuated vaccine within 28 days. No severe allergy to compounds similar to the study agents.
No prior or concurrent malignancy that could interfere with safety or efficacy assessment.
Not pregnant and not nursing.

schema.text: Two 28-day cycles; IT methotrexate days 1 and 15 each cycle; dexamethasone 20 mg before blinatumomab on day 1. Treatment starts within 14 days.

arms.label: Arm 1
arms.text: Blinatumomab continuous IV (28 mcg/day adults; 15 mcg/m²/day if <18, max 28) days 1-28 plus revumenib PO every 12 hours (270 mg if >40 kg, 160 mg/m² if <40 kg) days 4-28 of cycle 1 and days 1-28 of cycle 2.

Adults: allogeneic HCT allowed; non-transplant adults 18-54 recommended CALGB 10403, ≥55 low-intensity chemotherapy plus blinatumomab, per physician.

schema.label: Cohort B (single arm, age ≥55)
schema.text: Newly diagnosed untreated Ph-negative KMT2A-rearranged B- or T-ALL or ALAL. Feasibility run-in with revumenib de-escalation, then expansion. Induction (35 days): vincristine 1.5 mg/m² (max 2 mg; 1 mg/m² if ≥70) days 1, 8, 15, 22, dexamethasone 5 mg/m² twice daily days 1-7 and 15-21, daunorubicin 25 mg/m² days 1, 8, 15, IT cytarabine and IT methotrexate, revumenib days 8-28. If CR, CD19+ B-lineage, and no grade ≥3 revumenib toxicity: 2 cycles of blinatumomab 28 mcg/day plus revumenib (42-day cycles). T-ALL comes off after induction.

schema.label: Primary endpoint
schema.text: Cohort A: safety in run-in; MRD-negative CR by clonoSEQ after one cycle in MRD-positive participants, then MRD event-free survival (hierarchical). Cohort B: feasibility of revumenib with reduced-intensity chemotherapy.

eligibility: Cohort A: B-ALL or ALAL with KMT2A translocation documented locally (cytogenetics, FISH, or NGS); CD19 expression at any level at diagnosis; Ph-negative; no lymphoid blast crisis of CML or prior TKI for CML.

Cohort A: Morphological CR1 (marrow blasts <5%) after induction; trackable clonoSEQ clone or banked diagnostic sample available; not already known MRD-negative by clonoSEQ and not known to lack a trackable clone.
Cohort A: Age ≥1 (no upper limit); Zubrod/ECOG 0-2 or Lansky/Karnofsky 50-100. Adults may have had 1-3 cycles of induction/consolidation; children must enroll after induction.

Cohort A: No prior blinatumomab, menin inhibitor, CAR-T, or anti-CD19 antibody; no prior allogeneic HSCT; no systemic immunosuppressants other than leukemia chemotherapy (prednisone ≤10 mg/day allowed).
Cohort A: No relapsed or refractory marrow disease (≥5% blasts) or extramedullary involvement; no active CNS2 or CNS3 (prior CNS disease allowed if now CNS1).

Cohort A labs within 14 days: GFR ≥50 mL/min/1.73 m² (adults CrCl ≥50 mL/min), ANC ≥1 x 10^3/uL, platelets ≥100 x 10^3/uL, direct bilirubin ≤2.0 mg/dL (≤5x ULN with Gilbert's), ALT ≤5x ULN. LVEF ≥50% or shortening fraction ≥27% within 90 days.
Cohort B: Age ≥55, Zubrod/ECOG 0-2, newly diagnosed Ph-negative B- or T-ALL or ALAL with locally documented KMT2A translocation; no CML blast crisis or prior CML TKI.

Cohort B: No prior systemic therapy except hydroxyurea, steroids, retinoic acid, IT chemotherapy, or study-backbone induction already started if revumenib can begin by induction day 8; no prior allogeneic HSCT.

Cohort B labs within 14 days: CrCl ≥50 mL/min, direct bilirubin ≤2.0 mg/dL (≤5x ULN if Gilbert's or leukemia-related), ALT ≤5x ULN unless leukemia-related. LVEF ≥50% within 28 days. Lumbar puncture within 14 days; no bulky CNS involvement (CNS3c: facial palsy, brain or eye involvement, hypothalamic syndrome).
All: Strong CYP3A4 inhibitors and strong or moderate inducers (except corticosteroids) stopped 14 days before registration; recovered from major surgery ≥14 days.
All: QTcF ≤450 msec on screening ECG; NYHA class 2B or better if cardiac history or prior cardiotoxic therapy.

All: No uncontrolled infection; no oxygen >2 L/min, mechanical ventilation, or vasopressors (Cohort A); no clinically significant autoimmune disease (Cohort A). Able to take oral medication (NG/G-tube oral solution allowed).

HIV allowed with effective ART and undetectable viral load within 6 months; chronic HBV allowed with undetectable viral load on suppressive therapy; HCV must be cured or have undetectable viral load on treatment (Cohort A adults and all Cohort B).
No prior or concurrent malignancy that could interfere with safety or efficacy assessment.
Not pregnant and not nursing (negative pregnancy test within 7 days before treatment).

schema.label: Step 1: Screening and initial treatment
schema.text: Confirmed de novo stage IV oligometastatic (5 or fewer lesions) HER2-positive breast cancer. Physician's choice of NCCN/ASCO guideline-concordant systemic therapy for 12-24 weeks. One week is seven calendar days. Preferred regimens are those used for stage III disease.

schema.label: Step 2: Cohort assignment
schema.text: Response per section 5.2 is assigned to Cohort A and randomized 1:1. Progression or no response per section 5.2 is assigned to Cohort B.

schema.label: Cohort A randomization
schema.text: After randomization, continue NCCN/ASCO concordant systemic therapy to complete at least 1 year. Preferred regimens are those used for residual disease after neoadjuvant chemotherapy.

arms.label: Arm 1
arms.text: Definitive locoregional therapy to the breast and lymph nodes plus SRT to all metastatic sites, per section 7.2.a.

arms.label: Arm 2
arms.text: No surgery or radiation unless required for palliation, per section 7.2.b.

schema.label: Cohort B
schema.text: Physician's choice of NCCN/ASCO guideline-concordant HER2-directed systemic therapy, continued for at least 1 year or until disease progression, then follow-up.

eligibility: Step 1, disease: histologically confirmed de novo metastatic (AJCC stage IV, no prior breast cancer) HER2-positive breast cancer with 1 to 5 distant lesions. Confirm metastasis by biopsy of a distant site unless biopsy is not feasible or safe, in which case imaging and laboratory studies must show unequivocal metastasis. Confirm HER2 in the breast tumor and a metastatic site per NCCN guidelines version 4.2025. If bone HER2 is equivocal, or biopsy is not feasible or safe, breast-tumor HER2 is acceptable. If there is no breast lesion, confirm HER2 in at least one metastatic site.

Step 1, brain metastases are allowed when there are 5 or fewer intracranial lesions and each is no larger than 2 cm. The brain counts as one distant site. Brain imaging is not required without neurological symptoms, but symptom assessment and brain MRI are encouraged. No known leptomeningeal disease.

Step 1, prior therapy: either treatment-naive and planning to start standard HER2-targeted therapy, or already started it and completed at least 1 and no more than 3 cycles without progression. Baseline scans within 28 days before treatment starts.

Step 1: no investigational systemic therapy before disease progression. No whole-brain irradiation. Up to five brain metastases may have received SRS or SRT before or after systemic therapy starts. Small asymptomatic lesions may be observed if the regimen has CNS penetration.

Step 1, clinical: age 18 or older and Zubrod performance status 0-2. Known HIV requires effective antiretroviral therapy and an undetectable viral load within 6 months. Able to receive the physician's choice of standard HER2-targeted therapy per the package insert, physician judgment, and institutional guidelines.

Step 1: a candidate for definitive surgery and radiotherapy of locoregional disease, and able to receive ablative SRT to every metastatic lesion identified at baseline, in the treating physician's opinion.
Step 1: offered optional specimen banking (non-US sites are exempt). Informed consent is required. A legally authorized representative may consent when decision-making is impaired.

Step 2, Cohort A: register within 14 days of the staging scans done after Step 1. Those scans and breast imaging follow 12-24 weeks (at least 4 cycles) of initial systemic therapy and are within 14 days before Step 2. Use the same imaging modality as Step 1.

Step 2, Cohort A response: partial or complete response in the breast in the treating physician's opinion. A breast lesion at diagnosis needs a clinical response on breast imaging. Metastatic lesions are at least stable by RECIST and bone criteria. Brain metastases treated with SRS or SRT are at least stable by RANO-BM and do not require steroids. If there was no breast lesion at diagnosis, metastatic sites must show at least a partial response.

Step 2, Cohort A local therapy: still eligible for definitive surgery and radiotherapy of locoregional disease, and every metastatic lesion can receive ablative SRT. A lung lesion that resolves completely is not targeted, because dose buildup is not possible. A new sclerotic bone lesion after systemic therapy is not called progression, and such lesions are targeted with SRT.

Step 2, Cohort B: register within 14 days of staging and breast imaging after 12-24 weeks (at least 4 cycles), using the same modality as Step 1. Assignment requires stable disease or progression: progression in metastases by RECIST or bone criteria, or stable metastases with progression or no clinical response in the breast.
